title: Weight-Adjusted Gradients Reveal Parameter Importance and Failure Modes in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2607.10803v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding which parameters are influential in Large Language Models (LLMs) is central to improving their efficiency, reliability, and interpretability. We introduce Weight-Adjusted Gradients (WAG), a simple yet effective approach for estimating parameter importance that explicitly captures the interaction between model weights and first-order gradient information and identifies parameters that disproportionately influence model behavior, such as those responsible for collapse phenomena in LLMs. Across a range of models and settings, we show that WAG surfaces a tiny but critical subset of parameters (< 0.5 parts per million or 0.00005% of model size) whose modification leads to dramatic degradation in performance, indicating a novel failure mode. These findings also reveal a previously underexplored interplay between weights and gradients, suggesting that parameter importance cannot be fully understood through either signal

translated_title: 权重调整梯度揭示大语言模型中的参数重要性与失效模式
translated_abstract: 理解大语言模型（LLM）中哪些参数具有重要影响，是提升其效率、可靠性和可解释性的核心。我们提出了权重调整梯度，这是一种简单而有效的参数重要性估计方法，它显式地捕捉模型权重与一阶梯度信息之间的交互作用，并识别出对模型行为产生超比例影响的参数，例如那些导致大语言模型崩溃现象的参数。在多种模型和设置下，我们证明 WAG 能够揭示出一个极小但至关重要的参数子集（低于百万分之0.5，即模型规模的0.00005%），对这些参数进行修改会导致性能的急剧下降，这揭示了一种新颖的失效模式。这些发现还揭示了权重与梯度之间此前未被充分探索的相互作用，表明仅凭其中任何一个信号都无法完全理解参数重要性。
tldr: 提出权重调整梯度（WAG）方法，通过捕捉权重与一阶梯度的交互作用来估计参数重要性，发现仅修改极小一部分关键参数（不足模型规模的0.00005%）就会导致大语言模型性能急剧崩溃，从而揭示了一种全新的失效模式。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Weight-Adjusted Gradients (WAG), a method that captures the interaction between weights and first-order gradients to estimate parameter importance, revealing that modifying a tiny critical subset of parameters (<0.00005% of model size) causes dramatic performance degradation and exposing a novel failure mode in LLMs.
